questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Why is DNA replication described as semi-conservative?
options: each new molecule has one original strand and one new strand
only half the genes are copied
questions.answer: each new molecule has one original strand and one new strand
questions.hint: Think about what happens to the parent strands.

questions.subject: bio

options: unwinds the double helix and separates the strands
joins nucleotides into a new strand
cuts DNA into fragments for analysis
adds a primer at the 3' end
questions.answer: unwinds the double helix and separates the strands
questions.hint: It breaks hydrogen bonds between bases.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Which bonds does helicase break?
options: covalent bonds in the sugar-phosphate backbone
questions.hint: These bonds hold the two strands together.

options: it ensures the new strand has the correct base sequence
questions.answer: it ensures the new strand has the correct base sequence
questions.hint: A pairs with T, C pairs with G.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: If a template strand reads 5'-ATGCCA-3', what is the base sequence of the complementary strand, written 3' to 5'?
questions.hint: Pair each base: A–T, G–C.

it works only at low temperatures

bus-hl.topic: Motivation: Taylor, Maslow, Herzberg — HL: McClelland and Deci & Ryan

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which three needs does McClelland's acquired needs theory identify?
questions.hint: These needs are learned through life experience.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: In self-determination theory, which three basic psychological needs are identified?
questions.hint: Deci and Ryan focus on intrinsic motivation.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: An employee who prefers moderately challenging goals and regular feedback has a high need for…
questions.hint: McClelland: someone who wants to excel.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: An employee who values harmony and being liked by colleagues has a high need for…
questions.hint: Think about relationships.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: In McClelland's theory, which need describes the desire to influence and control others?
questions.hint: Often found in successful managers.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: In self-determination theory, what type of motivation comes from enjoyment of the task itself?
questions.hint: The opposite of motivation from external rewards.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Allowing staff to choose how they organise their own work mainly supports which need in self-determination theory?
questions.hint: Think about choice and control.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Training that helps workers master new skills mainly supports which need in self-determination theory?
questions.hint: Feeling effective and capable.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which Taylor-style practice would most likely reduce autonomy, according to Deci and Ryan?
questions.hint: Who decides how the work is done?

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: In Herzberg's theory, which factor is a motivator?
questions.hint: Motivators come from the job content.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which statement best reflects Maslow's hierarchy?
options: Lower-level needs must largely be met before higher needs motivate
Money is the only true motivator
questions.answer: Lower-level needs must largely be met before higher needs motivate
questions.hint: Think of the pyramid.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Deci and Ryan suggest that large extrinsic rewards for an already enjoyable task may…
questions.hint: Sometimes called the crowding-out effect.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which is a limitation of McClelland's theory for managers?
options: Needs are difficult to measure accurately
It ignores the need for achievement
It applies only to factory workers
It is based on piece-rate pay
questions.answer: Needs are difficult to measure accurately
questions.hint: How would a manager observe a 'need'?

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: A tech start-up is recruiting a sales manager. Using McClelland's theory, explain which need profile the business might look for.
questions.hint: Consider achievement and power in a target-driven role.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Explain how a hospital could use self-determination theory to improve the motivation of its nurses.
questions.hint: Address each of the three needs.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Evaluate the usefulness of Taylor's scientific management for a modern software company.
questions.hint: Compare routine tasks with creative work.

bus-sl.topic: Motivation theories: Taylor, Maslow and Herzberg

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which theorist is most associated with scientific management?
questions.hint: Think of time-and-motion studies in factories.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: According to Taylor, what mainly motivates workers?
questions.hint: He saw workers as 'economic beings'.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Name the payment system, favoured by Taylor, where workers are paid per unit produced.
questions.hint: Pay depends on output, not hours.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which level sits at the base of Maslow's hierarchy of needs?
questions.hint: What must a human have simply to survive?

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: What is the highest level of Maslow's hierarchy of needs?
questions.hint: Reaching one's full potential.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: A firm offers permanent contracts and a pension scheme. Which of Maslow's needs does this mainly satisfy?
questions.hint: Think about security and stability.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Team-building events and a staff canteen mainly address which of Maslow's needs?
questions.hint: Relationships with colleagues.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: In Herzberg's two-factor theory, which is a hygiene factor?
questions.hint: Hygiene factors prevent dissatisfaction but do not motivate.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: In Herzberg's theory, which is a motivator?
questions.hint: Motivators relate to the job itself and personal growth.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: According to Herzberg, what do hygiene factors prevent when they are met?
questions.hint: They do not create satisfaction on their own.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Job enrichment, giving workers more challenging tasks and responsibility, is most closely linked to which theorist?
questions.hint: Think about motivators in the work itself.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which is a common criticism of Taylor's approach?
options: It ignores workers' social and psychological needs
It gives workers too much autonomy
It is too expensive to measure output
questions.answer: It ignores workers' social and psychological needs
questions.hint: Is money the only thing people want from work?

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which is a limitation of Maslow's hierarchy?
options: People may not satisfy needs in a fixed order
It is based on piece-rate pay
questions.answer: People may not satisfy needs in a fixed order
questions.hint: Can someone seek esteem before feeling fully secure?

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: A call centre pays staff well but morale is low and staff turnover is high. Using Herzberg's two-factor theory, explain why higher pay may not solve the problem.
questions.hint: Separate hygiene factors from motivators.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage of using piece-rate pay in a clothing factory.
questions.hint: Consider output and quality.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Discuss whether Maslow's hierarchy is useful for a manager in a small café.
questions.hint: Think about applying it to real staff with different needs.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Which statement about an endothermic reaction is correct?
options: ΔH is positive and the surroundings cool down
ΔH is negative and the surroundings cool down
ΔH is positive and the surroundings warm up
ΔH is negative and the surroundings warm up
questions.answer: ΔH is positive and the surroundings cool down
questions.hint: System gains energy; surroundings lose it.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Bond breaking is…
questions.hint: Energy must be supplied to separate atoms.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: In an energy profile, what is the name of the highest-energy arrangement of atoms between reactants and products?
questions.hint: It sits at the top of the activation energy hill.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: For an exothermic reaction, how does the activation energy of the reverse reaction compare with the forward reaction?
questions.hint: The products start lower down the profile.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Calculate q in J when 75.0 g of water warms by 4.20 K. Give your answer to 3 significant figures. (c = 4.18 J g⁻¹ K⁻¹)
questions.hint: q = mcΔT; round at the end.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: 50.0 cm³ of solution (assume 50.0 g) warms by 6.8 K when 0.0250 mol of water forms in a neutralisation. Calculate ΔH in kJ mol⁻¹ to 3 significant figures, with the sign. (c = 4.18 J g⁻¹ K⁻¹)
questions.hint: Find q, convert to kJ, divide by moles.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: 0.500 g of ethanol (M = 46.08 g mol⁻¹) is burned. How many moles of ethanol is this? Give your answer to 3 significant figures.
questions.hint: n = m/M.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Burning 0.0109 mol of ethanol heats 200.0 g of water by 13.0 K. Calculate ΔHc in kJ mol⁻¹ to 3 significant figures, with the sign. (c = 4.18 J g⁻¹ K⁻¹)
questions.hint: q = 200.0 × 4.18 × 13.0, then divide by moles.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: The data booklet ΔHc of ethanol is about −1367 kJ mol⁻¹. A student obtains −997 kJ mol⁻¹. Which is the most likely main cause?
questions.hint: Consider a systematic error in an open flame experiment.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: In a calorimetry experiment, which assumption is usually made about a dilute aqueous solution?
options: It has the same density and specific heat capacity as water
questions.answer: It has the same density and specific heat capacity as water
questions.hint: This lets you use m = volume and c = 4.18.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: If the same neutralisation is repeated using double the volumes of both solutions at the same concentrations, the temperature rise will be…
questions.hint: Both the energy released and the mass heated double.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: What is the SI unit used for the standard enthalpy change of a reaction in IB Chemistry?
questions.hint: Energy per amount of substance.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Which statement about the stability of reactants and products in an exothermic reaction is correct?
options: The products are more stable than the reactants
The reactants are more stable than the products
questions.answer: The products are more stable than the reactants
questions.hint: Lower enthalpy means more stable.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Explain, in terms of bonds, why the combustion of methane is exothermic.
questions.hint: Compare energy absorbed and released.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: A student measures the enthalpy of neutralisation in a glass beaker without a lid. Evaluate the method and suggest two improvements.
questions.hint: Think about heat loss and the heat capacity of the container.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Sketch in words and explain an energy profile for an exothermic reaction, labelling Ea and ΔH.
questions.hint: Describe reactants, transition state and products.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: In an exothermic reaction, what is the sign of ΔH?
options: It depends on the temperature only
questions.hint: Energy is released to the surroundings.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: What happens to the temperature of the surroundings during an endothermic reaction?
questions.hint: Energy is taken in from the surroundings.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: What is the name of the minimum energy needed for a reaction to occur?
questions.hint: It is the 'hill' on an energy profile.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Which process is endothermic?
options: Neutralisation of an acid with an alkali
questions.hint: Which needs continuous heating?

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: On an energy profile for an exothermic reaction, the products are…
options: lower in energy than the reactants
higher in energy than the reactants
at the same energy as the reactants
questions.answer: lower in energy than the reactants
questions.hint: Where did the released energy come from?

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: In q = mcΔT for a reaction in aqueous solution, m usually represents the mass of…
questions.hint: What absorbs the heat and changes temperature?

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Give the specific heat capacity of water in J g⁻¹ K⁻¹ (to 3 significant figures).
questions.hint: It is given in the IB data booklet.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Calculate the heat energy, in J, absorbed by 50.0 g of water when its temperature rises by 6.0 K. (c = 4.18 J g⁻¹ K⁻¹)
questions.hint: Use q = mcΔT.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: 100.0 g of water warms from 21.0 °C to 31.0 °C. Calculate q in kJ to 3 significant figures. (c = 4.18 J g⁻¹ K⁻¹)
questions.hint: Find ΔT, then divide by 1000.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: A reaction releases 1.254 kJ of heat and 0.0250 mol of reactant is used. Calculate ΔH in kJ mol⁻¹ to 3 significant figures (include the sign).
questions.hint: Divide energy by moles and decide the sign.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: 25.0 cm³ of 1.00 mol dm⁻³ HCl reacts with 25.0 cm³ of 1.00 mol dm⁻³ NaOH. How many moles of water are formed?
questions.hint: Moles = concentration × volume in dm³.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: What are the standard conditions for enthalpy changes in IB Chemistry?
questions.hint: Room temperature in kelvin.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Why is an experimental enthalpy of combustion usually less exothermic than the data booklet value?
options: Heat is lost to the surroundings
Water has a low heat capacity
questions.answer: Heat is lost to the surroundings
questions.hint: Where else could the energy go?

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Which change would reduce heat loss in a simple coffee-cup calorimeter?
questions.hint: Think about the top of the cup.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Describe how you would draw an energy profile for an endothermic reaction, naming the key features.
questions.hint: Include reactants, products, Ea and ΔH.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Explain why the temperature rise of a neutralisation reaction is measured by extrapolating a temperature–time graph.
questions.hint: The reaction mixture loses heat while it reacts.

comp-hl.topic: B3.1 OOP for a single class: classes, objects and encapsulation

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which statement best describes the relationship between a class and an object?
options: An object is an instance created from a class
A class is an instance created from an object
They are two names for the same thing
An object defines the methods a class may use
questions.answer: An object is an instance created from a class
questions.hint: One blueprint, many houses.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which of the following is an instance variable rather than a local variable?
options: An attribute declared inside the class but outside any method
A variable declared inside a for loop
A variable declared inside the main method
questions.answer: An attribute declared inside the class but outside any method
questions.hint: Instance variables belong to each object.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which access modifier allows a member to be accessed from any other class?
questions.hint: It is the least restrictive modifier.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: State the term for a method that changes the value of a private attribute, often called setX.
questions.hint: It is the partner of an accessor.

questions.subject: comp
options: To distinguish the attribute from the parameter with the same name
questions.answer: To distinguish the attribute from the parameter with the same name
questions.hint: Two variables called owner are in scope.

questions.subject: comp
questions.hint: x and y refer to the same object in memory.

questions.subject: comp
questions.hint: p and q are two separate instances.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: A class has a private attribute temperature and a method setTemperature(double t) that rejects values below -273.15. Which OOP principle does this best demonstrate?
questions.hint: The class protects its own data from invalid values.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which is the best reason to provide a getter but no setter for an attribute?
options: To make the attribute read-only from outside the class
To make the program run faster
To allow any class to change it
To turn the attribute into a method
questions.answer: To make the attribute read-only from outside the class
questions.hint: Think about what outside code can and cannot do.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: A class Counter has a private int count and a method increment(). What is the most likely effect of increment()?
options: It adds 1 to count for that object
It adds 1 to count for every Counter object
questions.answer: It adds 1 to count for that object
questions.hint: Instance attributes belong to one object.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: In a UML class diagram, what does a minus sign (-) before an attribute indicate?
questions.hint: A plus sign (+) means the opposite.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which statement about constructors is correct?
options: A constructor has no return type and has the same name as the class
A constructor must return the new object with a return statement
A class can never have more than one constructor
questions.answer: A constructor has no return type and has the same name as the class
questions.hint: Look at BankAccount's constructor.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Construct a Java class Thermometer with a private double attribute reading, a constructor that sets it, and a getter. Write the class.
questions.hint: Follow the structure of the BankAccount class.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Explain how encapsulation can reduce errors when a large team of programmers works on the same system.
questions.hint: Think about who can change an object's data and how.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Compare a class and an object, using a real-world example to illustrate your answer.
questions.hint: Give one similarity or link and one difference.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Evaluate the decision to make every attribute in a class public in order to save time when coding.
questions.hint: Consider one benefit and at least two risks before reaching a judgement.

comp-sl.topic: B3.1 OOP for a single class: classes, objects and encapsulation

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: In object-oriented programming, what is a class?
options: A template that defines the attributes and methods of objects
A single variable that stores a number
A loop that repeats a block of code
A file that stores program output
questions.answer: A template that defines the attributes and methods of objects
questions.hint: Think of a blueprint for a house.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: What is an object?
options: A specific instance of a class
A keyword that ends a program
questions.answer: A specific instance of a class
questions.hint: One class can be used to create many of these.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: In a class Student, which of these is most likely to be an attribute?
questions.hint: Attributes store data; methods perform actions.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: In a class Student, which of these is most likely to be a method?
questions.hint: Look for something that performs an action.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: What is the name of the special method that is called automatically when a new object is created?
questions.hint: In Java it has the same name as the class.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which Java keyword is used to create a new instance of a class?
questions.hint: It appears before the constructor call, e.g. ___ Student(...).

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which access modifier makes an attribute visible only inside its own class?
questions.hint: This is the modifier used to hide data.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: What term describes bundling data with the methods that act on it and restricting direct access to that data?
questions.hint: It comes from the idea of putting something inside a capsule.

questions.subject: comp
questions.hint: Check which members are private.

questions.subject: comp
questions.hint: Look carefully at the condition inside deposit.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: What does the keyword this refer to inside a method or constructor?
options: The last object created in the program
questions.hint: It helps tell an attribute apart from a parameter with the same name.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: What is the main purpose of an accessor (getter) method?
options: To return the value of a private attribute
To change the access modifier of an attribute
questions.answer: To return the value of a private attribute
questions.hint: getBalance() is an example.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Two objects, a and b, are both created from the class Dog. Which statement is true?
options: Each object has its own copy of the instance attributes
They must have identical attribute values
Changing a's attributes always changes b's
Only one of them can call methods
questions.answer: Each object has its own copy of the instance attributes
questions.hint: Think about two different dogs with different names.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Explain one advantage of making the balance attribute private and providing a deposit method instead of letting other classes change balance directly.
questions.hint: Think about what deposit checks before changing the balance.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: A program models library books. Suggest two attributes and one method for a Book class, and state the purpose of the method.
questions.hint: Think about what every book has and something a library might do with it.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Outline why a programmer might create several objects from one class rather than writing separate code for each item.
questions.hint: Think about reuse and consistency.

econ-hl.topic: Business objectives and CSR — HL: costs and revenues

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Which condition gives the profit-maximizing level of output?
questions.hint: Produce until the extra cost equals the extra revenue.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Revenue maximization occurs at the output where:
questions.hint: Total revenue stops rising at this point.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: What term describes a firm aiming for a satisfactory level of profit rather than the maximum?
questions.hint: It combines 'satisfy' and 'suffice'.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: A firm sells 40 units at a price of $15 each. Calculate total revenue in dollars.
questions.hint: Total revenue = price × quantity.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: A firm's total revenue is $900 when it sells 60 units. Calculate average revenue in dollars.
questions.hint: Average revenue = total revenue ÷ quantity.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Total revenue rises from $500 to $560 when output rises from 20 to 23 units. Calculate marginal revenue in dollars per unit.
questions.hint: Marginal revenue = change in TR ÷ change in quantity.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: For a firm with a downward-sloping demand curve, which is correct?
options: MR equals AR at every output
questions.hint: To sell an extra unit, the price on all units must fall.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: The law of diminishing marginal returns applies:
options: In the short run, when a variable factor is added to a fixed factor
Only in the long run when all factors are variable
Only to firms in perfect competition
questions.answer: In the short run, when a variable factor is added to a fixed factor
questions.hint: Think about adding more workers to the same machine.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: A café with one coffee machine has a total product of 30 drinks per hour with 2 workers and 36 drinks per hour with 3 workers. Calculate the marginal product of the third worker in drinks per hour.
questions.hint: Marginal product = change in total product ÷ change in workers.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Diminishing marginal returns cause the short-run marginal cost curve to:
options: Rise after a certain level of output
questions.answer: Rise after a certain level of output
questions.hint: Each extra unit needs more of the variable factor.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Which statement about the MC and AC curves is correct?
options: MC cuts AC at the minimum point of AC
MC cuts AC at the maximum point of AC
questions.answer: MC cuts AC at the minimum point of AC
questions.hint: When the marginal is below the average, the average falls.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: A firm has total fixed costs of $200 and total variable costs of $400 at an output of 50 units. Calculate average total cost in dollars.
questions.hint: ATC = (TFC + TVC) ÷ Q.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: At the current output a firm's MR is $8 and MC is $11. To increase profit it should:
questions.hint: The last unit adds more to cost than to revenue.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Which is an example of corporate social responsibility?
options: Investing in renewable energy beyond legal requirements
questions.answer: Investing in renewable energy beyond legal requirements
questions.hint: CSR goes beyond the law.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Using a diagram you could draw, explain why the short-run average cost curve is U-shaped.
questions.hint: Link spreading fixed costs and the law of diminishing marginal returns.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Evaluate the view that firms should always aim to maximize profit rather than revenue or growth.
questions.hint: Consider stakeholders, the separation of ownership and control, and the long run.

econ-sl.topic: Alternative business objectives and corporate social responsibility

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: What is the traditional assumption about the main objective of firms in economic theory?
questions.hint: It is the objective used in standard models of the firm.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: A firm that aims to sell as much as possible in value terms, even if profit is lower, is pursuing:
questions.hint: Revenue is price × quantity.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: What term describes a firm aiming for a satisfactory level of profit rather than the maximum, to keep several stakeholders content?
questions.hint: It combines 'satisfy' and 'suffice'.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: What does CSR stand for?
questions.hint: It concerns a firm's behaviour towards society and the environment.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Which is an example of corporate social responsibility?
options: Reducing packaging waste beyond what the law requires
Paying the legal minimum wage only
questions.answer: Reducing packaging waste beyond what the law requires
questions.hint: CSR goes beyond legal obligations.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Which group is most likely to favour growth maximization over profit maximization?
options: Managers whose pay and status rise with firm size
Shareholders who want high dividends now
questions.answer: Managers whose pay and status rise with firm size
questions.hint: Think about the principal–agent problem.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Why might a firm aim for growth in market share in the short run?
options: To gain market power and economies of scale in the long run
Because growth always maximizes short-run profit
Because it is required by law
To reduce its number of customers
questions.answer: To gain market power and economies of scale in the long run
questions.hint: Think about the benefits of being large.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Satisficing is most likely to occur when:
options: Ownership and control are separated and stakeholders have different goals
A firm is run by a single owner who wants maximum profit
questions.answer: Ownership and control are separated and stakeholders have different goals
questions.hint: Think about managers, shareholders and workers wanting different things.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: A firm with CSR goals might choose to:
options: Pay suppliers in low-income countries a fair price
Cut safety training to lower costs
questions.answer: Pay suppliers in low-income countries a fair price
questions.hint: CSR is about ethical behaviour.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Which is a possible reason why CSR can increase a firm's long-run profit?
options: It can improve brand reputation and customer loyalty
It allows the firm to ignore regulations
questions.answer: It can improve brand reputation and customer loyalty
questions.hint: Think about how consumers react to ethical firms.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Which statement about revenue maximization is correct?
options: Output is higher than at the profit-maximizing level
Output is always lower than at the profit-maximizing level
Price is always higher than at the profit-maximizing level
It means the firm makes a loss
questions.answer: Output is higher than at the profit-maximizing level
questions.hint: To sell more, a firm usually lowers price and expands output.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: A large charity-linked café sets prices to cover costs and fund local projects. Its objective is closest to:
questions.hint: It does not seek the highest possible profit.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Explain why a firm might choose revenue maximization rather than profit maximization.
questions.hint: Think about market share, managers' rewards or economies of scale.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Explain one reason why a firm might engage in corporate social responsibility.
questions.hint: Consider both ethical reasons and business reasons.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Explain how the separation of ownership and control can lead firms to pursue objectives other than profit maximization.
questions.hint: Who owns the firm and who makes day-to-day decisions?

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Evaluate the view that firms should always aim to maximize profit.
questions.hint: Consider shareholders, other stakeholders and the long run before reaching a judgement.
